primary_cause: Lingering reaction to P&G's Feb 20 coronavirus warning that China disruption would hit Q revenue/profit
secondary_factors: Broad de-risking even in defensive consumer staples. 5.5% steep for defensive name
store_description: PG fell 5.5% which is steeper than expected for a defensive name. Investors were still repricing the implications of management's warning that China disruption would be material to the March quarter. The drop was likely a mix of that earlier warning plus the brutal COVID-driven market selloff.

primary_cause: No stock-specific catalyst. Broad COVID selloff
secondary_factors: General pharma/healthcare de-risking and litigation overhang already known
store_description: JNJ dropped only 3.2% less than many cyclicals which fits the idea that this was mostly index-level selling rather than a new company shock. No new earnings legal product or analyst event found in the prior 3 days.

primary_cause: Collapse in oil prices on COVID demand fears. Crude at one-year/13-month low
secondary_factors: Broad equity panic and recession fears
store_description: XOM's 6.0% drop is very consistent with the commodity tape. Oil was sliding hard as investors anticipated weaker transportation and industrial demand and energy was one of the most economically sensitive groups in the market.

primary_cause: Falling rates/yield-curve compression hurting bank earnings expectations
secondary_factors: Broad financial-sector risk-off selling
store_description: WFC fell 3.8% as the market moved to price in lower net interest income across banks if rates were cut and yields stayed pinned down. No fresh Wells-specific news item found in the Feb 24-27 window.

primary_cause: No clear Verizon-specific catalyst. Broad market selloff
secondary_factors: MWC cancellation as sector backdrop for 5G/telecom
store_description: VZ fell 3.6% which looks more like indiscriminate liquidation than a reaction to fresh company news. MWC's cancellation was relevant to the sector narrative but not large enough by itself to explain Verizon's move.

primary_cause: Rates collapse pressuring bank margin expectations
secondary_factors: Credit-risk concerns if virus slowed the economy
store_description: USB fell 4.3% which fits the move in regional and fee-sensitive banks as investors priced weaker loan growth narrower margins and a tougher macro outlook. No stock-specific catalyst stronger than the rates/recession channel.

primary_cause: Transport and global-commerce demand fears from COVID
secondary_factors: General cyclical-stock liquidation
store_description: UPS fell 3.7% as investors started to discount weaker international shipping volumes and broader supply-chain disruption. No fresh UPS-specific headline found.

primary_cause: Expected hit to rail volumes from virus-driven economic slowdown
secondary_factors: General industrial/cyclical de-risking
store_description: UNP's 3.7% drop fits the rail thesis. If manufacturing intermodal and trade volumes slow earnings estimates come down quickly. No company-specific press release or analyst action found.

primary_cause: No stock-specific catalyst. Broad market selloff
secondary_factors: Managed-care names not immune to forced de-risking
store_description: UNH fell 3.5% but no new earnings legal regulatory or policy headline found in the prior 3 days. Looks mostly like index and sector selling.

primary_cause: No stock-specific catalyst. Broad COVID selloff
secondary_factors: Concern about away-from-home beverage/snack demand and global distribution disruption
store_description: PEP fell 4.0% which is a bit large for a staple but no new Pepsi-specific shock found. Broad market liquidation plus concern that global consumer demand and channel mix could weaken.

primary_cause: Expected hit to ride demand from COVID/travel disruption
secondary_factors: High-beta still-unprofitable growth-stock selling
store_description: Uber's 5.8% drop makes sense as investors started discounting lower airport trips commuting volume and discretionary travel. No better company-specific catalyst found inside the Feb 24-27 window.

primary_cause: COVID fears around China exposure and production/supply-chain risk. Shanghai factory
secondary_factors: High-beta momentum unwind. MarketWatch explicitly tied weakness to COVID China fears
store_description: TSLA fell 4.4% on Feb 27 after already being hit earlier in the week with investors reassessing the risk that China disruptions could hurt production and deliveries.

primary_cause: No stock-specific catalyst. Semiconductor demand and supply-chain fears tied to COVID
secondary_factors: Cyclical tech selloff
store_description: TXN fell 3.3% which fits the market's growing concern that industrial and electronics demand would soften while Asian supply chains remained disrupted.

primary_cause: No stock-specific catalyst. Broad market liquidation
secondary_factors: General healthcare/life-science de-risking. Later benefited from COVID testing
store_description: TMO fell 3.3% but no negative company event found in the preceding 3 days. Marketwide risk-off move rather than Thermo-specific deterioration.

primary_cause: No stock-specific catalyst. Broad market selloff
secondary_factors: MWC cancellation and general media/telecom uncertainty from COVID
store_description: T fell 3.3% with no stronger company-specific negative development found in the immediate 3-day window. MWC cancellation likely contributed to sector unease but was secondary.

primary_cause: Expected collapse in mall traffic/retail footfall from COVID
secondary_factors: REIT selling tied to recession fears
store_description: SPG's 4.1% decline fits a straightforward pandemic-foot-traffic thesis. The market was starting to price the possibility that shoppers would stay home and tenants would struggle.

primary_cause: Rates collapse compressing Schwab's earnings outlook. Unusually rate-sensitive
secondary_factors: Financial-sector de-risking
store_description: SCHW fell 4.1% because Schwab's earnings are unusually sensitive to the rate environment. No better stock-specific trigger found than the violent move lower in yields and Fed expectations.

primary_cause: Ongoing repricing of Starbucks' China exposure and traffic risk. Late Jan warned 2000+ stores closed
secondary_factors: Feb 27 Reuters: 85% of China stores back open but damage done. Broad COVID market panic
store_description: SBUX fell 3.3% even though reopening progress was improving because the market was still wrestling with the earnings damage from the earlier large-scale closures in China and the risk that the outbreak would spread globally.

primary_cause: No stock-specific catalyst. Aerospace/industrial COVID repricing
secondary_factors: Travel and airline demand fears affecting broader aerospace complex
store_description: RTX fell 3.3% and the cleanest explanation is that investors were selling anything tied to aircraft demand industrial production and global supply chains.

primary_cause: COVID-driven fears around handset demand/5G launch cadence and supply chains
secondary_factors: MWC cancellation removed major launch/marketing venue. General semiconductor selloff
store_description: QCOM's 3.3% drop looks less like a fresh Qualcomm-only shock and more like a repricing of global smartphone demand plus industry disruption after the MWC cancellation.
